text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press at the weekend. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's 1996 corn crop is 9.6 million tonnes, of which 7.5 million will remain with farmers.
- European Investment Bank is to give a $35 million loan for the Bucharest heating authority.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The trade deficit was $890.3 million in the first 10 months of 1996, National Statistics Commission (CNS) data showed.
- October exports dropped by 19.8 percent from September and by 11.2 percent from October 1995.
COTIDIANUL
- The CNS put the average net wage at 374,633 lei in October.
- Bucharest has 30,000 unemployed but many of them refuse to work, the newspaper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- President Ion Iliescu told reporters he could run for a new term in office in the year 2000 elections.
- The Constitutional Court validated the results of the presidential election run-off won by Emil Constantinescu.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Newspaper director Ion Cristoiu donates a colour television tv set to Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea's parents after the press reported on Thursday that they had not heard that their son was the new premier.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Iliescu to head the outgoing Party of Social Democracy's parliamentary group.
- The National Peasant Party, National Liberal Party and Social Democratic Union have scheduled talks over the weekend to form the new government.
COTIDIANUL
- Romania's former opposition has control over parliament with 58.2 percent of seats in both chambers.
ZIUA

- President-elect Emil Constantinescu is expected to be sworn in twice: once in front of Romania's parliament, to get official investment and a second time in the Transylvanian historical town of Alba Iulia, on the national day, December 1.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- Constantinescu pleaded for national reconciliation of all political forces, saying it was the only way to overcome the hardships ahead. ($= 3,509 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
